output.brief: The wrong expiry dates did not come from the operators or the printer upgrade. The printer records show every Veltranol job before 4 Oct carried a 24-month shelf life and printed correctly, including jobs run by the new agency operators after the firmware change. From 4 Oct 22:10 onward, every job received a 36-month shelf life in the data sent to the printer. No operator overrode anything, and the camera passed every carton because it only checks print against the job. The ERP shows Regulatory Affairs entered 36 months on 3 Oct, but dated to take effect only from March 2027. The 24-month value is still the one in effect. So the line integration service sent the future value early. The vendor says it cannot do that, so that claim needs testing. The wrong dates affect Line 1 day shift too, with two lots in the warehouse. The director's plan would punish the wrong people and leave the fault in place. Do this now: correct the ERP record, extend the hold to all Veltranol lots since 4 Oct, add a second-person expiry check at each setup, and check other products with future-dated shelf-life edits (two found). Ask the vendor and IT to reproduce the early-value behaviour. Confidence is fairly high. Other products remain unchecked.
